summary.text: Senior Frontend Engineer with 6+ years of Angular and TypeScript, leading the frontend of a B2B fintech platform.

Focused on frontend architecture, performance and accessibility: migrated a production app to standalone components and Signals, cut the initial bundle by 38% and built WCAG 2.1 AA components used by three teams.

bullets.text: Lead the frontend of a B2B invoicing platform and a team of 4 engineers, owning frontend architecture, the shared component library and code-review standards.
Migrated the app from NgModules to standalone components and Signals over two quarters, feature by feature, without pausing product work.
Built a shared Angular component library of 32 components, documented in Storybook and used by 3 product teams.
Cut the initial bundle size by 38% with route-level lazy loading and by removing an unused charting library.
Made the library components meet WCAG 2.1 AA, with keyboard support, focus management and ARIA labels.
Added Cypress E2E tests for the invoice flow to GitLab CI.
Built a live shipment map updated over WebSockets for about 1,200 active vehicles, using RxJS throttling to keep the UI smooth.
Rebuilt the driver-assignment screen with NgRx, cutting the steps to assign a driver from 6 to 3.
Raised unit test coverage of the core dispatch services from 20% to 70%.
Built a zoneless Angular 20 budgeting app with signal-based state, offline storage in IndexedDB and an installable PWA.
Built a REST API with Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL, with JWT auth and Docker Compose.

paragraphs: I'm applying for the AI-native xEngineer (with Frontend core) role at Wix. I'm a Senior Frontend Engineer with 6+ years of Angular and TypeScript, and I lead the frontend of a B2B invoicing platform at Lumen Ledger.

Much of my work is the frontend architecture you describe. I migrated our production app to standalone components and Signals without pausing product work, built a 32-component library that three teams use, and cut our initial bundle by 38%. Our components meet WCAG 2.1 AA, and the core invoice flow is covered by Cypress tests in CI.

I want to be clear about where I would grow. My production experience is in Angular rather than React, and my Node.js work so far is a side project: a REST API with Express and PostgreSQL. I learn new approaches by building with them, as I did with a zoneless Angular app before bringing Signals to work.
I would welcome the chance to talk about how I could contribute to your Frontend Engineering group.
